summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would confirm the Bureau of Meteorology's power to accept paid advertisements on its website.
The Director of Meteorology would have to publish guidelines about which kinds of ads are allowed and could ban ads that harm the Commonwealth or the Bureau.
The bill would also validate any actions taken before it starts and make nine minor updates to wording in the Meteorology Act 1955.
changes: Gives the Director of Meteorology explicit authority to include paid advertising on the Bureau's services.
Requires the Director to develop and publish advertising guidelines, with power to prohibit ads not in the public interest.
Adds paid advertising to the list of services for which the Bureau can charge a fee.
Validates any actions taken before the bill commences to remove doubt about their legality.
Updates nine places in the Meteorology Act 1955 to modernise language and correct syntax.
summary.affected: The Bureau of Meteorology and its director are affected.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Introduced the Meteorology Amendment (Online Advertising) Bill 2014, following a 12-month trial of advertising on the Bureau of Meteorology's website recommended by the 2011 Munro review, to explicitly empower the Director of Meteorology to accept paid advertising and publish guidelines on acceptable ad content.

speeches.speaker: Mark Butler
speeches.brief: Supported the Meteorology Amendment (Online Advertising) Bill 2014 formalising online ads on the Bureau of Meteorology's website, which received about 500 million hits last year, but criticised the government's cutting of 58 bureau staff, including closing the Launceston office, following the Munro review's nearly $60 million package for extra meteorologists and hydrologists.

speeches.speaker: Philip Ruddock
speeches.brief: Declared that the Corporations Amendment (Simple Corporate Bonds and Other Measures) Bill 2014 and the Meteorology Amendment (Online Advertising) Bill 2014 were referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Supported the Meteorology Amendment (Online Advertising) Bill, recounting Watkin Tench's 1791 record of 109 degrees Fahrenheit heat in Sydney, and argued new advertising revenue is needed given Australia pays about $1 billion a month in interest on government debt, citing the bureau's own data showing cyclone numbers have decreased and global temperatures plateaued for the last 16 or 17 years.
